questions.question: Q1 What does RDMA stand for?

explanations.b: Correct. RDMA enables direct memory-to-memory data transfers without CPU involvement.

questions.question: Q2 What is the all-reduce operation?

answers.b: Aggregating local results from all nodes so every node has the global result

explanations.b: Correct. All-reduce combines local results and distributes the aggregated result to all nodes.

questions.question: Q3 What is a gradient in AI training?

answers.a: The slope of the loss function used to update model weights

explanations.a: Correct. Gradients indicate how to adjust model parameters to minimize loss.

questions.question: Q4 Why is synchronization necessary in distributed training?

answers.a: To keep all GPU clocks identical
answers.b: To ensure all nodes have consistent model weights

explanations.b: Correct. Without synchronization, model replicas would diverge.

questions.question: Q5 What is kernel overhead in TCP/IP communication?

answers.b: CPU time spent copying data between user space and kernel space

explanations.b: Correct. TCP/IP requires multiple memory copies through the kernel.

questions.question: Q6 What is a straggler node?

answers.a: A node with extra computing power
answers.b: A node that completes its work slower than others, delaying the entire cluster

explanations.b: Correct. Stragglers slow down synchronous operations because all nodes must wait for the slowest.

questions.question: Q7 In a ring all-reduce with N nodes, data completes the ring in how many steps?

explanations.b: Incorrect. N-1 steps for reduce, N-1 for broadcast.
explanations.c: Correct. Ring all-reduce requires 2(N-1) communication steps.

questions.question: Q8 How does RDMA bypass kernel overhead?

answers.b: By transferring data directly between GPU VRAM and the NIC hardware

explanations.a: Incorrect. RDMA eliminates CPU involvement entirely.
explanations.b: Correct. RDMA uses DMA to move data without kernel memory copies.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Compression is not the mechanism.

questions.question: Q9 What is network injection speed?

answers.a: The speed at which a node can place data onto the network
answers.b: The speed of CPU cache access
answers.c: The rate of network switch failures

explanations.a: Correct. Injection speed determines how fast a node can transmit data.

questions.question: Q10 Why is distributed training needed for large AI models?

answers.a: Single GPUs have sufficient memory and compute for any model
answers.b: Large models exceed single-GPU memory and compute capacity

explanations.a: Incorrect. Modern LLMs exceed single-GPU capacity.
explanations.b: Correct. Distributing across multiple GPUs enables training models too large for a single device.
